He played college basketball for [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]] after transferring from [[Northeast Mississippi Community College]]. == High school career == Buchanan is the son of Stephanie Latiker and has a younger brother, Shunn, who plays for [[New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball|New Mexico State]]. He grew up in [[Madison, Mississippi]], and attended [[Madison Central High School (Mississippi)|Madison Central High School]] where he was a standout basketball player. As a senior, he scored 23 points in the 6A playoffs to defeat defending champion [[Murrah High School]].{{cite news |last1=Dumlao |first1=Ros |title=Slam-dunk effort: Buchanan's play leads Madison Central in 6A |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/high-school/2014/02/26/slam-dunk-effort-buchanans-play-leads-madison-central-in-6a/5827279/ |accessdate=January 13, 2020 |work=[[Clarion Ledger]] |date=February 25, 2014}} Buchanan was not highly recruited and chose to attend [[Northeast Mississippi Community College]].{{cite news |last1=Cleveland |first1=Rick |title=In this Madison family, March Madness is real |url=https://mississippitoday.org/2019/03/22/in-this-madison-family-march-madness-is-real/ |work=Mississippi Today |date=March 22, 2019}} == College career == Buchanan averaged 14 points and 5.7 rebounds as a freshman at Northeast Mississippi and helped the Tigers capture the [[National Junior College Athletic Association]] (NJCAA) Region 23 title and reach the national tournament. Buchanan was a MACJC All-State selection as a freshman. As a sophomore, he averaged 18.4 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.3 assists, 1.7 steals, and 1.5 blocks per game, shooting 45.8 percent on field goals and 31.5 percent from beyond the arc. Buchanan had his best performance in the NJCAA Region 23 title game with a career-high 34 points on 11-of-17 shooting. He was a NJCAA All-American and signed with [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]].{{cite web |title=Buchanan Becomes Seventeenth Tiger to Earn All-American Recognition |url=http://www.nemcc.edu/buchanan-becomes-seventeenth-tiger-to-earn-all-american-recognition/ |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Community College]] |accessdate=January 13, 2020 |date=April 17, 2017 |archive-date=January 13, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200113223026/http://www.nemcc.edu/buchanan-becomes-seventeenth-tiger-to-earn-all-american-recognition/ |url-status=dead }} As a junior at Murray State, Buchanan averaged 9.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, and 1.6 steals per game. He teamed with [[Ja Morant]] to lead the Racers to a 26–6 record and appearance in the 2018 NCAA Tournament.{{cite web |title=OVC Basketball Media Day Powered by Vectren Video: Murray State |url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2018/10/26/mens-basketball-ovc-basketball-media-day-powered-by-vectren-video-murraystate.aspx |website=[[Ohio Valley Conference]] |accessdate=January 13, 2020 |date=November 1, 2018}} As a senior, Buchanan was named to the First Team All-[[Ohio Valley Conference]] as well as conference Defensive Player of the Year.{{cite press release|url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2019/3/4/murray-states-morant-and-buchanan-belmonts-muszynski-and-byrd-earn-2018-19-ovc-mens-basketball-top-honors.aspx |title=Murray State's Morant and Buchanan, Belmont's Muszynski and Byrd Earn 2018–19 OVC Men's Basketball Top Honors |publisher=[[Ohio Valley Conference]] |date=March 5, 2019 |accessdate=March 5, 2019}} He started all of his 33 games and averaged 13.0 points, 4.2 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.82 steals per game, helping lead the Racers to the 2019 NCAA Tournament. After the season, Buchanan competed in the Dos Equis 3X3 National Championship.{{cite news |title=Buchanan set to play in 3-on-3 event at Mall of America |url=https://www.murrayledger.com/sports/buchanan-set-to-play-in--on--event-at/article_9ebcf07a-510c-11e9-aa29-3745d60b161a.html |accessdate=January 13, 2020 |work=[[Murray Ledger]] |date=March 28, 2019}} As a 12 seed, Murray State defeated [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette]] 83–64 behind 14 points and six rebounds from Buchanan. He finished his career at Murray State with 722 points scored, 110 career steals and 63 starts in his 65 career games.{{cite news |last1=Kendall |first1=Nick |title=Former Racer Buchanan signs with Memphis Hustle |url=https://thenews.org/2019/10/20/former-racer-buchanan-signs-with-memphis-hustle/ |accessdate=January 13, 2020 |work=The Murray State News |date=October 20, 2019}} In two seasons at Murray State, Buchanan shot 48.4% from the field, 32.4% from behind the arc and 70.1% from the free throw line.{{cite news |last1=Marlowe |first1=Edward |title=MSU's Buchanan bound for Grizzlies summer league |url=https://www.paducahsun.com/sports/murray_state_sports/msu-s-buchanan-bound-for-grizzlies-summer-league/article_fe966a50-b667-5df6-a325-b993097486c6.html |accessdate=January 13, 2020 |work=[[Paducah Sun]] |date=June 23, 2019}} == Professional career == ===Memphis Hustle (2019–2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2019 NBA draft]], Buchanan joined the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] in the NBA Summer League. On October 17, Buchanan signed a one-year contract worth $898,310 with the Grizzlies.{{cite news|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Shaq of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite news |author1=Edward Marlowe |title=MSU's Buchanan relishes time with Summer League Grizzlies |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/99050630/ |access-date=4 April 2022
